senses.gloss: made for a very wide public
gloss_distractors: made by hand in small batches
senses.definition: Made and priced to sell to very large numbers of ordinary people.
senses.caution: Said about a brand that wants to seem special, it can sound like cheap or plain. As a noun, say the mass market.
senses.example: The first version is for hospitals, and we will only go mass market once the price drops below a hundred dollars.

cues.text: A startup that sells a costly device to hospitals plans a cheaper version that ordinary families could buy in any store.
A luxury brand's board worries that selling through discount chains will make the label look common.
You explain why a phone maker aims its basic model at hundreds of millions of first-time buyers rather than a few experts.
A friend complains that a once-rare sneaker brand now sells in every shopping centre in town.

distractors: Made to order for one customer.
Made in small numbers to test an idea before a real launch.
Priced high on purpose so that owning it shows the buyer has money to spare.
Sold only to other companies through long contracts, and never to members of the public directly.
